note_claims.claim: The patient has had a cough and coryza for 4 days and increased work of breathing since yesterday.
The patient has had a coryza and cough for 4 weeks.
The patient's temperature has been up to 37.9 °C.
The patient has been breathing fast since yesterday.
The patient has been feeding about half his usual amount since yesterday.
The patient has had four wet nappies in 24 hours, which is usually 6–7.
The patient has no history of apnoea (the older sister had an apnoea with bronchiolitis two years ago).
The patient has no history of cyanosis.
The patient was born at 39 weeks with no neonatal problems.
The patient has no cardiac or respiratory history.
The patient's immunisations are up to date.
The patient has taken Calpol once yesterday.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's temperature is 37.8 °C.
The patient's respiratory rate is 54 times a minute.
The patient's heart rate is 150.
The patient's oxygen level is 95 percent in air.
The patient has mild subcostal recession.
The patient's capillary refill is under two seconds.
The patient is alert and looking around.
The patient's weight is 8.2 kg (50th centile).
The patient has bilateral fine crackles and wheeze.
The impression is Bronchiolitis with moderately reduced feeding.
The patient is borderline for referral (feeds about 50%).
The plan is to give small, frequent feeds and use saline nose drops before feeds.
The patient is advised that the illness may worsen over the first three to five days.
The patient should be reviewed if not improving in one week.
Safety-netting advises calling GP or 111 urgently if feeds fall below half, no wet nappy for 12 hours, or if the patient seems more tired and floppy.

transcript_facts.fact: Arlo has had a runny nose and a cough for four days.
Arlo's breathing has been going really fast since yesterday.
Arlo is seven months old.
Arlo had a temperature of 37.9 this morning.
Arlo is taking most of his bottles.
Arlo is only managing about half of each bottle since yesterday.
The father did the night feeds.
Arlo keeps pulling off to breathe.
Arlo had four wet nappies in the last 24 hours.
Arlo usually has six or seven wet nappies.
Arlo's sister had an apnoea with bronchiolitis two years ago.
There was no apnoea with Arlo.
Arlo did not go blue or very pale.
Arlo brought up a bit of milk after coughing.
Arlo was born at 39 weeks with no problems.
Arlo has no heart or lung problems.
Arlo's immunisations are up to date.
Arlo has taken Calpol once yesterday.
The father smokes, but only outside, never in the house.
Arlo's temperature is 37.8.
Arlo's respiratory rate is about 54 times a minute.
Arlo's heart rate is 150.
Arlo's oxygen level is 95 percent.
Arlo is pulling in a little under his ribs when he breathes, indicating extra effort.
Arlo's capillary refill is under two seconds.
Arlo is alert and looking around.
The clinician can hear crackles and some wheeze on both sides of Arlo's chest.
The findings fit with bronchiolitis, a common virus in babies.
Arlo is working a bit harder to breathe.
Arlo's feeding is down to about half, which is right on the line.
Arlo's oxygen is okay and he is alert.
The clinician thinks it is reasonable to look after him at home for now.
The clinician advised giving Arlo smaller feeds more often.
The clinician advised using saline drops in his nose before feeds to help clear it.
Bronchiolitis often gets worse over the first three to five days before it gets better.
If Arlo has any pauses in his breathing, goes blue, or is really struggling to breathe, he should call 999.
If Arlo is taking less than half his usual feeds, has no wet nappy for 12 hours, or seems more tired and floppy, he should call 111 straight away, even overnight.
